newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds retain strength,waiting for leads.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds retain strength,waiting for leads.

text.p: *Bonds nudge ahead after firm opening, but trade remains light and in narrow ranges in absence of major local data until next week, and until U.S. provides fresh direction.
*May producer prices up 0.2 pct, up 0.8 pct over year.
Australian bonds had improved slightly on their firmer opening, but trade was quiet and held to narrow ranges as the market waited for direction this week from the U.S. Treasury market.
"A quiet start to the week -- that's been shown through the futures market," one trader said.

The expectation of a near-term rate cut is providing the market with a solid underlying tone, and it is expected to retain that tone ahead of next week's second quarter wage and inflation data. But until then local data is scarce, which traders say will keep the market's focus offshore.
Treasuries were boosted on Friday by a tame June producer price index suggesting inflation pressures remained contained, which also gave the local market its firm start to the week.
This week the market will be looking first to June U.S. retail sales figures on Tuesday and consumer prices on Wednesday for clues as to how the U.S. economy is travelling.

There are some minor local data this week, which is expected to be supportive of the market's expectation of a low inflation result next week. The first of these, manufacturing output prices for May, rose 0.2 percent, to be up 0.8 percent over the year, figures showed on Monday.

Spreads remain narrower on the day, reversing some of Friday's widening, and are expected to remain well-bid in the lead up to the wage and inflation data next week. The yield curve flattens slightly, reversing some of the steepening in the second half of last week.
